tasks.short: Check each supplier and agency invoice against the order, goods receipt or hours, then record it in AFAS.

steps.what: Pick invoices from the AP mailbox and register them in AFAS
Look up the purchase order and goods receipt for each invoice
Compare lines, quantities and prices; post clean matches for approval
Check agency invoices against portal hours and split the g-rekening share
Chase mismatches with the buyer, site manager or supplier

loop.input: match exception with invoice text, order lines and receipt
loop.output: likely cause (price, quantity, missing receipt, wrong order) and a draft query to buyer or supplier
loop.check: cause must cite the differing fields; draft is never sent without the bookkeeper
loop.stop: one pass per exception; low confidence or no cited field goes to the bookkeeper unclassified
loop.why_not_simpler: causes are stated in free text on PDFs and in mails, which rules cannot read

tasks.design: Switch on AFAS Profit UBL intake, Scan & herken and line-level three-way matching with set tolerances, so one-to-one matches are posted and released for approval without a touch. A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform reads agency portal hours, checks agency invoices, proposes the g-rekening split and posts only differences to a review queue. A small model step classifies the remaining exceptions and drafts the query for the bookkeeper to send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Many invoices arrived as PDF, goods receipts were registered late at the sites, and agency hours lived in three portals outside AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts one-to-one matches; AI coding makes the small agency-hours job cheap to build.
tasks.still_hard: Late or missing goods receipts at the warehouses and agency invoices that do not line up with approved hours stay a people problem.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a price or hours difference is acceptable, and settling it with a site manager or agency without souring the relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly check of every agency invoice against approved hours and g-rekening split, instead of spot checks at month end

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops opening matched invoices and spends the week on exceptions and on setting match tolerances and supplier master data with the controller.

reach.learn: How disputes are logged so AP and AR use the same cause codes
Which hours count as approved, so the agency check uses the same source

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts and approves one-to-one matches
AFAS Scan & herken turns a PDF into an e-invoice and finds the supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN; gaps are filled by hand
Noordhaven can limit chain liability by paying the wage tax and VAT share into the agency's g-rekening
Measured touchless shares often disappoint because of own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions

assumptions: Purchase orders and goods receipts are kept in AFAS for most non-agency spend
At least two of the three agencies can export hours by file or API
unknowns: Share of invoices that arrive as UBL today
How quickly sites register goods receipts
Which agencies offer an API or structured export
Current g-rekening percentages agreed per agency
research_questions: What share of last quarter's invoices would have matched one-to-one in AFAS with a 1% tolerance?
Do the agency portal hours equal the hours on the agency invoices in at least 90% of weeks?
How many exceptions per week remain after matching, and what are their top three causes?

tasks.short: Key debits and credits into AFAS and total accounts in Excel to check they balance.

steps.what: Key journal entries from Excel workings into AFAS
Export balances and total accounts in Excel to check
Post recurring entries such as rent, leases and accruals
Make corrections and reclassifications found in review

tasks.design: Replace hand keying with a fixed Excel journal template that a script validates (balanced, valid accounts, cost centres, VAT codes) and posts through the AFAS import connector as unapproved entries for a second person to release. Recurring entries move into AFAS periodic journals, and the Excel totalling is replaced by a Power BI balance check page on the nightly AFAS extract.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workings came in many Excel layouts, and nobody owned a template or import routine, so keying was the safe default.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS connectors and AI-assisted coding make a validated import script a few days of work; Power BI already reads AFAS nightly.
tasks.still_hard: Getting colleagues to use one template, and the corrections that need judgement on accounts and periods.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which account and period an odd item belongs to and spotting an entry that balances but is wrong.
tasks.altitude: Less keying; the bookkeeper releases imported batches and handles corrections, with no new decision rights.

reach.learn: Which accruals recur and can move to AFAS periodic entries

evidence.claim: Recording and posting with standard accounting software is deterministic; the 10-key and Excel arithmetic goes away with structured data
Log every decision with its data and let people handle exceptions

assumptions: AFAS import connector for journal entries is licensed and enabled
Power BI extract includes ledger balances
unknowns: How many manual journal entries are keyed per month
Whether AFAS periodic entries are already in use
Who is allowed to release imported journals
research_questions: How many manual journal lines per month come from Excel workings, and from how many layouts?
Could a single template cover 80% of them?
How many corrections per month trace back to keying errors?

tasks.short: Assign ledger account, cost centre and VAT code to transactions and summarise records for the close.

steps.what: Code invoices without an order to account, cost centre and VAT

loop.input: invoice lines, supplier, past coding of this supplier
loop.output: suggested ledger account, cost centre, site and VAT code with a reason
loop.check: account and cost centre must exist and be allowed for the supplier group; VAT code must fit supplier country and reverse-charge rules; deviation from supplier default is flagged
loop.stop: one suggestion per line; failed check or new supplier goes to the bookkeeper uncoded
loop.why_not_simpler: supplier defaults in AFAS cover fixed suppliers, but mixed invoices and new suppliers need reading the line text

steps.what: Record bank costs, credit notes and small receipts
Build summaries of costs per site and open items in Excel
Answer controller and site questions about how items were coded

tasks.design: Set supplier default coding in AFAS for fixed suppliers and add a bounded model step that suggests coding for the rest, checked against an allowed-account table and VAT rules, with the bookkeeper confirming. Bank lines and costs are booked by AFAS bank rules, and the Excel summaries become a Power BI page per site on the nightly extract, with drill-down to the coded line and the reason.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coding depended on each bookkeeper's memory of suppliers and sites, and own accounts and VAT codes made rule sets incomplete.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding suggestions from vendor history are now common in AP tools, and a checked suggestion step can be built cheaply around AFAS data.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed invoices across sites and new suppliers; touchless rates often fall short of vendor claims.
tasks.human_edge: Judging the right account and VAT treatment for unusual purchases and explaining the choice to the controller or auditor.

ambition.what: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a weekly cost-per-site view they never had

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper confirms suggestions and maintains supplier defaults and the allowed-account table, a decision right shared with the controller.

reach.learn: Which cost centres and splits FP&A needs so coding feeds the forecast directly
What reasons per coded line the auditor wants to see

evidence.claim: Coding suggested from vendor history, reviewed and confirmed by the team; per-invoice time from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds
Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions per administration block touchless processing
AFAS matches bank lines on reference, IBAN and invoice number by rules

assumptions: Two or more years of coded invoice history exist in AFAS
Power BI licences can be extended to site managers
unknowns: Share of invoices with a fixed supplier default today
Number of administrations and VAT code sets in AFAS
Whether invoice data may be sent to a model endpoint under the current AVG processing agreement
research_questions: On last year's invoices, how often would supplier history alone have given the correct account and VAT code?
How many coding corrections did the controller or auditor make last year?
Do site managers want a weekly cost view, and would they act on it?

tasks.short: Copy figures from agency, expense and other side journals into AFAS or Excel data sheets.

steps.what: Download agency hours, invoice lists and expense sheets
Retype or paste figures into an Excel data sheet
Post the sheet into the AFAS general ledger
Tie totals of sheet and ledger and fix rejected lines

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on the governed data platform fetches agency and expense files, maps them to AFAS accounts and cost centres with a maintained mapping table, and posts them through the AFAS connector as unapproved journals. The job ties source totals to posted totals, sends rejected lines to the bookkeeper in Teams, and the bookkeeper releases each batch.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each source had its own layout and no IT capacity existed for small interfaces, so Excel was the glue.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small file-to-connector jobs cheap; AFAS connectors accept journal imports.
tasks.still_hard: Agency portals change layouts without notice and some may only offer manual downloads.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a source file is incomplete or a mapping no longer fits, and deciding whether to post or hold.

ambition.what: Flex labour cost posted weekly per site instead of once at month end

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops copying and owns the mapping table and the batch release; days to close shorten because flex costs are already in.

reach.learn: How weekly posted flex costs can replace their own estimates
Which worker and site identifiers keep agency data and AFAS aligned

evidence.claim: Agency invoices checked against time records with only differences to a person is the proposed Noordhaven case
Transfers between structured sources are deterministic software work

assumptions: A governed data platform with scheduling and secrets exists or can be provided by IT
AFAS journal import connector is available
unknowns: Which journals are still transferred by hand besides agency and expense data
Whether agency contracts allow automated portal access
Works council view on processing flex-worker hours data in a new job
research_questions: List every side journal copied into AFAS last month and its volume; which three cover 80%?
Can each agency deliver a stable export or API?
How many rejected or corrected lines does a manual transfer produce today?

role.altitude: The bookkeepers move from keying and matching invoices to running the exceptions queue, releasing batches and owning match tolerances, supplier master data, coding defaults and the agency mapping table with the controller.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: shared dispute cause codes between AP and AR
Payroll Specialist: one source of approved flex-worker hours
FP&A Analyst: weekly site and flex labour costs feeding the forecast
Controller: audit evidence per coded and matched line
skills_to_grow: Configuring AFAS matching, Scan & herken, bank rules and periodic entries
Maintaining master data and mapping tables as controlled data
Reading Power BI exception and cost pages
Chain liability, g-rekening and VAT reverse-charge rules
Reviewing model suggestions critically and logging decisions
role.ambitious_version: Every agency invoice is checked weekly against approved hours with the g-rekening split done automatically, most supplier invoices post without touch, and the three bookkeepers spend their time on supplier data quality and exceptions, cutting days to close.
